source.title: Acalabrutinib Versus Ibrutinib in Previously Treated Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: Results of the First Randomized Phase III Trial
source.short_title: Acalabrutinib Versus Ibrutinib in Previously Treated CLL
source.packet_gap: The article references a Data Supplement and Study Protocol, but neither is present in the packet or identity-matched Drive outputs. The complete published main article is usable for the reported main-text methods, efficacy, safety, limitations, figures, and tables.

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Atoms were extracted from the supplied main article. Missing online Data Supplement and Study Protocol were not reconstructed. Figure 3 subgroup estimates were extracted directly from the source figure.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial prospectively compared acalabrutinib with ibrutinib in previously treated CLL to test noninferior progression-free survival with improved tolerability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This phase III trial prospectively compared the efficacy and safety of acalabrutinib with ibrutinib in patients with previously treated CLL.

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults with previously treated CLL requiring therapy, ECOG performance status 2 or less, and centrally confirmed del(17p) and/or del(11q); key exclusions included significant cardiovascular disease, vitamin K antagonist treatment, prior BTK or BCL-2 inhibitor therapy, and proton-pump inhibitor requirement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Eligible patients were age 18 years or older, had previously treated CLL, required therapy by International Workshop on CLL criteria

population.label: Trial eligibility population
exclusion_criteria: Warfarin or equivalent vitamin K antagonist
Prior BTK or BCL-2 inhibitor treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial randomized 533 patients, 268 to acalabrutinib and 265 to ibrutinib, across 124 centers in 15 countries; median age was 66 years, 45.2% had del(17p), 64.2% had del(11q), and the median number of prior therapies was two.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 533 patients were randomly assigned at 124 centers in 15 countries to receive acalabrutinib (n = 268) or ibrutinib (n = 265)

atoms.canonical_statement: Acalabrutinib was given orally at 100 mg twice daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: receive oral acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily

atoms.canonical_statement: Ibrutinib was given orally at 420 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: or ibrutinib 420 mg once daily

atoms.canonical_statement: This was a randomized, multicenter, open-label, phase III noninferiority study registered as NCT02477696.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is a phase III, randomized, multicenter, open-label, noninferiority study (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02477696).

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible patients were randomized 1:1, with stratification by del(17p) status, ECOG performance status, and number of prior therapies; crossover was not permitted.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: randomly assigned eligible patients in a 1:1 ratio

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment was open label, but the independent review committee centrally assessed progression and response while blinded to treatment assignment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An independent review committee (IRC) centrally assessed progression and response data in a blinded manner.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was IRC-assessed progression-free survival, defined as time from randomization to disease progression or death from any cause.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary end point was IRC-assessed PFS, defined as the time from random assignment until disease progression or death from any cause.

outcome.definition: Time from random assignment until disease progression or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Prespecified secondary endpoints were any-grade atrial fibrillation, grade 3 or higher infections, Richter transformation, and overall survival.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary end points were the incidences of atrial fibrillation (any grade), infections (grade 3 or higher), and Richter transformation and overall survival

concept.text: Prespecified secondary efficacy and safety endpoints

outcome.definition: Any-grade atrial fibrillation; grade >=3 infection; Richter transformation; overall survival

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety was assessed from first dose until 30 days after the last dose or the start of new anticancer therapy, whichever occurred earlier, using CTCAE version 4.03.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Safety was assessed by AE, laboratory, and clinical assessments across the treatment-emergent period

atoms.canonical_statement: The PFS noninferiority margin was an acalabrutinib-to-ibrutinib hazard ratio of 1.429; about 500 patients provided 80% power at a one-sided 0.025 significance level.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: hazard ratio (HR) scale margin of 1.429 (noninferiority margin of 30%)

atoms.canonical_statement: A prespecified gate-keeping sequence tested PFS noninferiority first, followed by superiority for atrial fibrillation, grade 3 or higher infection, Richter transformation, and overall survival; after a failed superiority step, subsequent P values were descriptive.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The gate-keeping strategy was implemented to control the family-wise error rate at the 0.05 level

atoms.canonical_statement: Efficacy analyses used all randomized patients and safety analyses used all patients who received at least one study-drug dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Efficacy analyses were performed for the intent to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients). Safety analyses ... all patients who received at least one dose

atoms.canonical_statement: After 40.9 months median follow-up, median IRC-assessed PFS was 38.4 months in both arms and the hazard ratio was 1.00 (95% CI 0.79 to 1.27), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: median IRC-assessed PFS was 38.4 months in both arms

outcome.definition: Time from randomization until disease progression or death from any cause

quantitative_result.original_result_text: median IRC-assessed PFS was 38.4 months in both arms; HR 1.00; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.27

atoms.canonical_statement: Because the PFS curves crossed at about 33 months, a restricted mean survival time sensitivity analysis over 55 months found an acalabrutinib-minus-ibrutinib difference of 1.1 months (95% CI -2.17 to 4.36), supporting noninferiority.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the difference in RMST between acalabrutinib and ibrutinib was 1.1 months (95% CI, -2.17 to 4.36)

outcome.definition: Time from randomization until disease progression or death from any cause

quantitative_result.original_result_text: difference in RMST between acalabrutinib and ibrutinib was 1.1 months (95% CI, -2.17 to 4.36)

atoms.canonical_statement: Median overall survival was not reached in either arm; 63 of 268 acalabrutinib patients and 73 of 265 ibrutinib patients died, with HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.59 to 1.15).

atoms.canonical_statement: IRC-assessed overall response was 81.0% with acalabrutinib and 77.0% with ibrutinib, an absolute difference of 4.0 percentage points calculated from the reported rates.

atoms.canonical_statement: Any-grade atrial fibrillation or flutter occurred in 9.4% with acalabrutinib and 16.0% with ibrutinib; the directly reported incidence difference was -6.6 percentage points (95% CI -12.2 to -0.9; P=.02).

atoms.canonical_statement: The cumulative incidence of atrial fibrillation or flutter favored acalabrutinib, HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.32 to 0.86).

atoms.canonical_statement: The cumulative incidence of hypertension favored acalabrutinib, HR 0.34 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.54); any-grade hypertension events were 9.4% versus 23.2%.
Any-grade cardiac events occurred in 24.1% with acalabrutinib and 30.0% with ibrutinib; cumulative incidence favored acalabrutinib with HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.52 to 1.00).

atoms.canonical_statement: The study did not analyze survival outcomes by cause of treatment discontinuation, so it could not determine whether differences in adverse-event discontinuation affected survival.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: survival outcomes were not analyzed by cause of treatment discontinuation

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identified the open-label design as a limitation because patients and treating physicians knew the assigned treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Other study limitations include the use of an open-label versus blinded study design

atoms.canonical_statement: The study population consisted of patients with relapsed CLL with del(17p) or del(11q), which the authors described as high-risk prognostic features.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study was performed in patients with relapsed CLL with del(17)(p13.1) or del(11)(q22.3)

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that acalabrutinib was noninferior to ibrutinib for PFS and had improved safety, with fewer atrial fibrillation events and adverse-event discontinuations, while maintaining similar efficacy in previously treated CLL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: acalabrutinib is non-inferior in PFS and provides improved safety with fewer atrial fibrillation events and discontinuations because of AEs versus ibrutinib
